archetype.name: Playoff Team (goaltending-first)
archetype.definition: A team whose elite goaltending and penalty kill lift an even-strength game that is roughly break-even into a playoff-caliber record, with very little margin if the saves dry up.

report.headline: Sorokin and the PK carry an average 5-on-5 team toward the playoffs
report.take:
The Islanders are 11-6-5 with 27 standings points, ninth on the site's board and third in a Metropolitan Division led by Carolina. That puts them on a 101-point pace, which would be their best finish in years. It looks like a good season. Look past the standings, though, and the formula is familiar. At 5-on-5 they are a middle-of-the-league team: a 49.9% xGF share (18th) and a 49.0% CF share (21st). They allow 28.1 shots a game, 24th in the league. The defense ranks sixth in goals allowed because the goaltending is second in GSAx at 13.4 and the penalty kill is fourth at 85.1%.

That is the same team from history. Last season's club got 40.1 GSAx and a fifth-ranked defense out of a 48% xGF share and turned it into 91 points. In 2022-23, 41.1 GSAx produced 93. Ilya Sorokin is the engine again: .918, 10.2 GSAx, eighth among 72 goalies. The difference this year is the other end of the ice. The offense, which ranked 22nd or worse in every one of the last five seasons, sits 15th. Bo Horvat has 21 points in 22 games, third on the centers tab. And the power play is still bad: 17.2%, 29th, more than five points under the league average.

The numbers hide how much of the offensive improvement is shooting luck. The skaters are converting 13.4% of their shots, sixth in the league and well above the 9.8% league norm. Paired with a .910 save percentage, that gives an all-situations PDO of 104.4, fourth in the league. The 5-on-5 PDO is 102.3. The record itself isn't lucky: Pts vs Goal Diff is -0.1, so the +8 differential has been converted fairly. But the differential leans on percentages, not on territory.

The last five games (4-0-1, 22 goals for, 11 against) are the high-water mark. They came against a soft stretch and on a shooting heater. Expect the scoring to cool back toward the team's career norm. The goaltending is the part that has proven repeatable here, and it should keep this team comfortably in the playoff race even after the regression.

strengths.title: Goaltending saves more than anyone's
strengths.body: Team GSAx of 13.4 ranks second, and Sorokin alone accounts for 10.2 of it with a .918 save percentage. This has been the franchise's foundation: the 2022-23 and 2025-26 teams both topped 40 GSAx. Sorokin's share of it is the most bankable thing on the sheet. Varlamov's .889 is the softer half of the tandem.

strengths.title: An elite penalty kill
strengths.body: The PK is killing 85.1% of penalties, fourth in the league and nearly eight points better than average. Part of that is the goalie, the last line of any kill. But the club also ran an 84.2% kill in 2021-22 and 80.8% last season, so it is not a pure fluke. Expect it to settle a little but stay well above average.

strengths.title: Horvat drives the top line
strengths.body: Horvat has 9 goals and 21 points in 20.84 minutes a night. He has a 52.6% xGF share while the team as a whole sits under 50%, which is why the site ranks him third among centers. He also has 7 power-play points on a unit that otherwise struggles. He is the one forward whose underlying numbers back up the scoring.

concerns.title: Scoring built on hot shooting
concerns.body: The skaters are shooting 13.4%, sixth in the league and well above the league's 9.8%. Every previous season in the sheet had an offense ranked 22nd or worse. With a sub-50% shot-attempt share, there is no volume to fall back on when the percentage normalizes. The middle-of-the-pack offense is likely to slide back toward the bottom third.

concerns.title: Outplayed at even strength
concerns.body: An xGF share of 49.9% and a CF share of 49.0% describe a team that trades chances evenly at best. It concedes 28.1 shots a game, 24th in the league. The sixth-ranked defense is mostly goaltending: the structure lets in volume and the goalies clean it up. That works only as long as the goalies stay at this level.

concerns.title: The power play is chronic
concerns.body: The PP is converting 17.2%, 29th, more than five points below the league average. This is a recurring problem, not a slump: 15.8% in 2022-23, 12.6% in 2024-25 and 16.5% last season. It is the main reason a team this good at preventing goals keeps finishing as a bubble club.

trend.note: A rough patch of losses and overtime defeats around the start of November has given way to 4-0-1 in the last five. Over that run they scored 4.4 a game and allowed 2.2, the best stretch of the season. It came against mostly weaker opponents and on a shooting surge.

weekAhead.headline: A homestand against three sub-.500-caliber clubs, then a back-to-back
weekAhead.body:
The schedule is kind. Toronto (27th on the site), St. Louis (15th) and Winnipeg (21st) all visit, before a trip to Philadelphia (24th) the night after the Winnipeg game. None of the four outrank the Islanders. Toronto and Winnipeg have shaky goaltending and allow a lot of shots: Winnipeg's 31.6 a game is the most in the league. That suits a team leaning on finishing. Philadelphia sits 29th in xGF share.

The Winnipeg-Philadelphia back-to-back is the likeliest spot for a Varlamov start. His .889 is a real step down from Sorokin, so the Flyers game is the one to circle as a potential stumble even though Philadelphia is the weakest team underneath. Anything less than a winning week here would be a warning sign.

keyMatchups.title: Toronto's power play vs the PK
keyMatchups.body: Toronto's only real strength is a power play converting 25.7%, sixth in the league. It meets the Islanders' fourth-ranked kill. Toronto's GSAx is -5.2, so the Islanders' strong special-teams defense against a leaky goaltending situation tilts this one clearly their way.

keyMatchups.title: A slumping PP gets Winnipeg's PK
keyMatchups.body: Winnipeg kills just 72.5% of penalties, 24th, and gives up the most shots in the league. If the Islanders' 29th-ranked power play is going to find life, this is the night. The Jets' defense has also been worst in the league against defensemen.

keyMatchups.title: Horvat against Philadelphia's centers
keyMatchups.body: Philadelphia ranks 32nd in points allowed to centers, giving up 0.54 a game against an expectation of 0.33. That sets up well for the Islanders' one high-end center to close the week. The catch is the back-to-back, both for his legs and for the goalie behind him.

weekAhead.watch: Whether the power play finally converts against Winnipeg's weak kill. That would be a scoring source that doesn't depend on a 13.4% shooting percentage holding up.

restOfSeason.body:
The goaltending is the sustainable part. Sorokin has backed seasons like this before, and the penalty kill should stay well above average. What will regress is the shooting: 13.4% against a 9.8% league mark, on a team that doesn't generate more shot attempts than it allows. As that fades, the offense should drift back toward the lower third, where it has lived for five years. The 101-point pace will soften with it.

Without a fix on the power play, the most likely outcome is another goaltending-driven season in the low-to-mid 90s in points. That is enough to stay in the Metropolitan playoff picture, but not to threaten Carolina. Upside depends on the PP climbing toward league average. Downside depends on Sorokin's workload: Varlamov's starts have been noticeably weaker.
swingFactors: How far the 13.4% shooting rate falls
Any improvement on the 29th-ranked power play

confidence.note: 22 games is a small sample. But the goalie-driven profile matches the last several seasons closely.
